Either an inherited term, or a Slavic borrowing. Çabej deems it as inherited from Proto-Indo-European, listing Proto-Slavic *dolto (“chisel”) and Latin dolō (“to hew”) as cognates, and linking it internally with deltinë (“clay”). Çabej's arguments are based on the lack of archaic borrowings from Slavic into Albanian; in this case, a borrowing would necessitate linguistic exchange prior to Slavic liquid metathesis. From an unattested root *pjé + -të, from Proto-Indo-European *peth₂-, with the meaning going from "in flight" > "in the air" > "above, upwards". First attested in 1555 by Buzuku: "se u ëngriti duoi em e it pjetë përmal, e duojtë taj e kishnë ëngjëruom e prunjishnë për të ënfalë timit." Orel claims it to be an unattested noun, meaning "widening, sky", though this is purely speculative as aside from two mentions by Buzuku, the word is found nowhere else, except in its derived terms.
